clue.text: Obtain conclusion from judge consistent with law

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its closing letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of judge
licit means lawful, permitted

explanation.surface: A litigant wants a ruling from a judge that sticks to the law.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit a response or fact is to draw it out, which is to obtain it.

clue.text: Change layout in part of theatre for matinee

indicators.note: a part of the following words holds the answer, running unbroken across them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of theatre, all of for, and the start of matinee

explanation.surface: Seating in one section of a theatre is rearranged for an afternoon show.
explanation.definitionFit: To reformat a document or disk is to give it a new layout or structure.

clue.text: Repeatedly note tree rot

blocks.note: B is a musical note
the alder is a waterside tree
a second note: a dash is the long signal in Morse code

explanation.surface: Someone keeps writing down that a tree is decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeatedly' tells you to use note twice, with a different sense each time: first the musical note B, then the long Morse signal, the dash, after the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot in its informal sense is nonsense, and balderdash is senseless talk.

clue.text: Recent event started by shot that makes the papers

blocks.note: recent means new
a sprint is a track race begun by the starter's pistol

explanation.surface: A fresh story begun by a gunshot is the kind of thing that makes the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes the papers' suggests getting into the news; literally, newsprint is the cheap paper newspapers are printed on.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the stock from which newspapers are physically made.

clue.text: Country without any end or beginning

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are dropped from the country's name

blocks.note: a European country
the word any, taken from the end of the country

explanation.surface: A land with no limits in either direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without any end' reads as endless, but it means remove ANY from the end; 'or' is a link and 'beginning' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is the seed or origin of something, as in the germ of an idea.

clue.text: Kind of cake that's positively motivating

definitions.note: the answer names a kind of cake as a modifier: carrot cake

blocks.note: first meaning: the vegetable that names a spiced sponge
second meaning: a reward offered as an incentive

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense comes from the carrot and stick: a reward rather than a threat, hence 'positively'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrot cake is a familiar bake, and a carrot dangled before a donkey is the classic incentive by reward.

clue.text: Set of definitions a lexicographer finally put in magazine

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
things put in something end up inside it, so these letters go within the periodical

blocks.note: a glossy is a magazine printed on shiny paper
taken as written
the last letter of lexicographer

explanation.surface: A dictionary-maker's word list ends up printed in a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of terms with their meanings, a collection of definitions.

clue.text: Sheltered location in main general hospital area

blocks.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general
a ward is a section of a hospital

explanation.surface: A quiet spot in the main area of a general hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'principal', but here it is the old word for the open sea, so the definition is a sheltered side at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side of a ship or island faces away from the wind, so it is the sheltered side on the sea.

clue.text: Parliament providing plan for consumers

blocks.note: first meaning: a legislative assembly, such as Japan's
second meaning: a controlled eating regime

explanation.surface: A legislature produces a strategy for shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Several national assemblies are called a Diet, and a diet is also an eating plan for those who consume food.

clue.text: Pupil's situation, being subject to examination

definitions.text: Pupil's situation, being subject to examination

blocks.clueFragment: Pupil's situation, being subject to examination
blocks.note: surface reading: a schoolchild is in the position of sitting exams

blocks.clueFragment: Pupil's situation, being subject to examination
blocks.note: setter's reading: the organ where the dark centre of the eye sits, which an optician inspects

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' is not a student but the opening in the iris, and the examination is an eye test.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye's globe carries the pupil and is what an eye doctor looks at closely.

clue.text: Old clue's convoluted, second is totally clear

indicators.note: something convoluted is twisted and tangled, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A solver complains that an old clue is tangled while another is perfectly clear.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudless sky is completely clear, without a single cloud.

clue.text: Economist said to be making money in his country no longer

definitions.text: money in his country no longer

indicators.note: said means spoken, so it is the sound of the economist's name that counts

blocks.note: Karl Marx, the German economist

explanation.surface: An economist is reported to be earning money in a country he has left.
explanation.walkthrough: Marx was German, and the mark was Germany's currency until the euro replaced it in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: German marks were the national currency of Marx's homeland and are no longer in use.

clue.text: Possibly watch male entering bank

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so the man's letter sits within the bank

blocks.note: a bank of seats or oars is a tier, a row
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Perhaps keep an eye on a man going into a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' shows the definition is by example: a watch is one kind of timer.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a timepiece, one example of a device that measures time.

clue.text: Events at sea get a tar excited

indicators.note: an excited state is agitated and stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Races on the water get a sailor worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: A tar is an old word for a sailor, which keeps the surface nautical.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, events held on the water.

clue.text: Produce text for another good entertainer, correctly pronounced

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken out, so the sound of the word for correctly is what matters

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a host entertains guests
right means correctly

explanation.surface: A good performer writes words for someone else, with the right pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: To ghostwrite is to write material that appears under another person's name.

clue.text: Crows, for example, about all I messed up in sport

indicators.note: messed up means jumbled into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
about means surrounding, so the birds wrap around the jumbled letters

blocks.note: crows are an example of birds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Crows mess everything up during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue game played on a cloth table, a sport of skill.

clue.text: Funny programme that's twice cut in series it completes

definitions.text: Funny programme that's twice cut in series it completes

blocks.clueFragment: Funny programme that's twice cut in series it completes
blocks.note: surface reading: a comedy show censored twice during its run

blocks.clueFragment: Funny programme that's twice cut in series it completes
blocks.note: setter's reading: a comedy genre whose two words are each shortened to make its usual name, and which is in series

explanation.walkthrough: The common short form takes the first three letters of each of the two words, so the full name is 'cut' twice; such shows run in series.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the full name of the sitcom, a comedy series built around characters in a recurring setting.

clue.text: Holder of weapon, person who won't strike poet

blocks.note: a scab is a worker who breaks a strike
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: An armed man refuses to hit a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests a blow, but here it is industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: A scabbard is the sheath in which a sword or dagger is carried.

clue.text: Skilled but penniless, one supported by hard work

indicators.note: having no penny means losing the coin's abbreviation from the word

blocks.note: expert means skilled
the Roman numeral for one
something resting on another is supported by it

explanation.surface: A capable but broke person is kept afloat by toil.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for a penny, so 'penniless' removes it. In a down clue, 'one supported by' puts I on top of what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Exertion is strenuous physical or mental effort, which is hard work.

clue.text: Drink beer, mostly chilled, when it's hot inside

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the last letter of that word is dropped
inside places the letter for hot within the word for chilled

blocks.note: ale is a beer
cool means chilled
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Drink a beer, mostly cold, when the weather is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is a general term for intoxicating drink.

clue.text: Lots of people who sail, we hear, do so for pleasure

definitions.note: 'so' refers back to sail, so this means sail for pleasure

indicators.note: we hear means it is the spoken sound of the word for groups that counts

blocks.note: crews are the teams who work ships

explanation.surface: Many sailors go out on the water purely for enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition borrows 'sail' from the wordplay: 'do so' means sail.
explanation.definitionFit: To cruise is to travel by sea on a voyage taken for leisure.

clue.text: Daily crime

blocks.note: a daily is a newspaper; this one is the Financial Times, with its article and abbreviated name

explanation.walkthrough: A daily in crosswords is often a newspaper; the Financial Times is known as the FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the crime of stealing property.

clue.text: Experienced altered state with first of drugs

indicators.note: something altered has been changed, so these letters are rearranged
first of picks out the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of drugs

explanation.surface: Someone knew an altered state of mind, brought on by drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tasted something, such as success, is to have experienced it.

clue.text: A spinner's taken over

blocks.note: taken as written
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: A slow bowler has been replaced or hit for runs in an over.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture misleads: a spinner here is a spinning top.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on top of, so it is equivalent to over.

clue.text: Bow's sound piece of yew

indicators.note: sound points to how the word for bend is said, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: bow as in bending at the waist, rhyming with cow

explanation.surface: An archer's bow is made from good yew wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Longbows were made of yew, so 'bow' and 'yew' make an archery picture; 'yew' could even sound like 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bough is a main branch of a tree, so a piece of a yew.

clue.text: Cool, paradoxically, about duck making other bird's call

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for warm wraps around the zero

blocks.note: in slang both cool and hot mean fashionable, a paradox
a duck is a score of nought in cricket

explanation.surface: A cool bird around a duck produces a different bird's cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paradoxically' warns that the word for cool is its apparent opposite; in cricket a duck is a score of zero, shaped like O.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoot is the call of an owl, a bird other than the duck.

clue.text: Purge extreme characters from party – the British complaint

indicators.note: purging the outermost letters strips each following word of its first and last letters

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political purge of extremists from a party, which is a British complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word of 'party – the British' loses its two ends, not just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthritis is a painful joint disease, and a complaint is an ailment.

clue.text: Ponders, when confused, to get answer

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thinks hard when puzzled in order to find a solution.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to reply, to give an answer.

clue.text: Preserve bit of golf course that's best avoided when driving

blocks.note: to pot food is to preserve it in a jar
a golf course is divided into holes

explanation.surface: Keep a section of the golf course that players should steer clear of when teeing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' suggests a golf drive; the definition is about driving a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a hole in a road surface that drivers try to steer around.
